PhD Candidate | Geospatial Data Scientist
University of Connecticut
I use satellite Earth observation, GeoAI, and spatial modeling to study Arctic infrastructure, settlement change, permafrost risk, and data-scarce built environments.

title: Home
text:
Research Areas


Arctic Infrastructure Risk
Estimating climate-related exposure and damages to buildings and infrastructure across permafrost regions.


GeoAI for Building Detection
Developing deep learning methods to map buildings in remote and data-scarce Arctic regions.


Nighttime Lights & Settlement Change
Using satellite nighttime lights to characterize post-Soviet settlement decline and activity change.


Remote Sensing for Human Geography
Combining Earth observation, population data, and spatial modeling to study human-environment systems.

title: Home
text:
Featured Projects

HABITAT: Arctic Building Footprints
A pan-Arctic building inventory developed using deep learning and high-resolution satellite imagery.


Permafrost Degradation Damages
Estimating mid-century damages to Arctic buildings from permafrost degradation.


Russian Arctic Settlement Change
Using nighttime lights and settlement population records to identify severe demographic and infrastructure decline.
